reportedCompletion.summary:
FIXED — but NOT the way the title asks, and the difference is the point.

The title says fleet:launch-on-plan 'rejects valid cross-hive goal work', which reads as a request to let the call through. I did not do that and it should not be done. The refusal comes from the scoped-superuser transport clamp in _mcp-handler.ts, which its own source calls 'a real security boundary against cross-workspace TENANT data' (P-006/P-007/P-008). Widening it would let any papercusp-scoped session launch fleets into any sibling hive. The guard is correct; the reporter was at the wrong door.

What WAS defective is that the refusal was a DEAD END. The same code block already emits tailored cross-hive routes for two tools — work_items:claim ('discovery:pots → pot:request_work') and work_items:get (a per-id-family retry explanation) — but for launch-shaped tools it emitted a bare 'harness_forbidden: harness "sidestage" is outside this session's hive "papercusp".' and nothing else. The reporter held a goal worklist that legitimately named another hive's plan, got that bare 'no', and stopped, recording it as blocked work. A boundary that is right to refuse is still wrong to refuse without naming where the work CAN go.

FIX — packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/transport/_mcp-handler.ts:
- Added CROSS_HIVE_LAUNCH_TOOLS (fleet:launch-on-plan, fleet:create, capability:launch-agent) + an exported crossHiveLaunchHint(toolName, scopeHive), following the file's existing ReadonlySet+predicate convention (cf. SUPERUSER_GLOBAL_FLAG_ADMIN / isSuperuserGlobalFlagAdmin).
- Wired it into BOTH harness_forbidden refusal sites. The handler builds that text in two separate places (the spawn-context clamp and the dispatch clamp) with duplicated hint logic; a fix applied to only one is half-live and looks complete.
- The hint names two verified routes — run the fleet from a session scoped to that hive, or discovery:pots → pot:request_work (verified to exist; its own description is 'ask the peer to do something in its domain', becoming a work_item in the peer's backlog).
- It also pre-empts the obvious wrong next move: `hive` on fleet:launch-on-plan selects which shared hive's federated SEAT-OFFERS to place onto for placement:'remote'. That is a cross-MACHINE knob, not a cross-hive harness escape, so retrying with it cannot lift the refusal. I checked this rather than assumed it (launch-on-plan.ts resolveRemotePlacementHive / the `hive` arg doc).

I also ruled OUT fleet:request_remote_spawn as the route: it is cross-MACHINE (asks a machine that delegated seats to spawn from them), a different axis entirely, so naming it would have sent the next reader down a second dead end.
